quests.sentence: Honestly? I'd already made up my mind before you even finished the sentence.
quests.hint: The decision was made before the other person even finished speaking, an earlier point.
quests.explanation: Had made up (shortened to 'd made up) is the past perfect form, showing this happened before another past event.

quests.sentence: You made a fair point, though.
quests.hint: This is a simple completed observation about something already said.
quests.explanation: Made is the simple past form, describing a completed past action.

quests.sentence: Give it a minute — I'll come around.
quests.hint: This is a decision or promise being made right now, in response to the conversation.
quests.explanation: Will come around is the will-future form, describing a decision made in the moment.

quests.sentence: Morale's been low for a while, and it's starting to show in the numbers.
quests.hint: Focus on the first half — a situation that began in the past and is still true now.
quests.explanation: Has been (shortened to 's been) is the present perfect form, describing a situation continuing up to the present.

quests.sentence: Turnover doubled compared to this time last year.

quests.explanation: Doubled is the simple past form, describing a completed change measured against a past reference point.

quests.sentence: Something has to change before this situation gets any worse.

quests.sentence: They hadn't spoken in years, not since the wedding.

quests.sentence: Their mother's funeral was the first time they'd been in the same room since.

quests.sentence: Whether they'll patch things up now remains to be seen.

quests.sentence: The draft reads fine on its own, but it hasn't earned that ending yet.

quests.sentence: Earlier versions tried something bolder and frankly worked better.

quests.sentence: Readers will forgive a lot if the characters feel real.

quests.sentence: Confidence hasn't fully recovered since the last downturn.

quests.sentence: Analysts had underestimated the speed of the rebound.

quests.sentence: By most accounts, growth will have slowed considerably by year's end.

quests.explanation: Will have slowed is the future perfect form, describing a change expected to be complete by a future point.

quests.sentence: Nobody had given this team a real shot before the season started.

quests.sentence: They proved everyone wrong, one upset at a time.

quests.sentence: History will remember this run long after the trophy's been forgotten.

quests.sentence: Early results showed a marked improvement within weeks.

quests.sentence: If the trend holds, the therapy will have reached full approval within two years.

quests.sentence: Something in me had already let go, long before I admitted it.

quests.sentence: From here, I'm just going to see where it leads.

quests.sentence: By the time anyone thought to check on him, he'd been gone for hours.

quests.sentence: The note he left explained everything, in the end.

quests.sentence: Whatever comes next, they'll figure it out together.

quests.sentence: She'd spent the better part of a decade proving people wrong, and she wasn't about to stop now.

quests.sentence: The doubters had gone quiet a long time before the trophy ever showed up.

quests.sentence: Whatever comes next, she's already won more than most people ever will.
